WF-03 Step 3 (implement the fix) for ISS-0119. The design artefact `lib/letflow/design/iss-0119-status-file-readability.md` (1,004 lines) PASSED the Step 2 gate on re-gate pass 3 after two FAILs and two rework iterations. It is specific by design -- §11 is the exact file list, §10 carries post-edit text for every instruction site, §4 quotes the required header verbatim, §8 gives the normative verification commands. BUILD WHAT IT SPECIFIES. Where the design gives exact text, use that text; do not improve it. If you believe the design is wrong about something, report it in result.issues rather than silently diverging -- it has been through two independent gate passes and a disagreement is worth surfacing, not absorbing.

ORCH ROUTING DECISION ON §11's SPLIT: §11 offers ORCH the discretion to let Step 4 own the two test files. ORCH takes it. YOUR scope is 2 CREATED + 9 MODIFIED:
  CREATE: docs/status/requirement_status.v2.yaml, docs/status/requirement_status.index.yaml
  MODIFY: docs/status/requirement_status.yaml (EOF footer append ONLY), CLAUDE.md, docs/agents/instructions/core-directives.md (3 sites: :173, :290, :328), .claude/agents/doc-updater.md (3 sites), .claude/agents/release-validator.md (1 site), docs/agents/AGENT_SYSTEM.md (3 sites), docs/agents/workflows/WF-02_requirement_implementation.md (2 sites), docs/agents/protocols/TASK_QUEUE.md (2 sites), docs/anti-patterns.md (1 rewrite + 1 new entry)
  DO NOT CREATE: test/support/status_history.ex or test/docs/requirement_status_invariants_test.exs -- TEST-DESIGNER owns both at Step 4 per §7/§7.1. Your job is to make the design's world exist so those tests can assert against it.

THE ONE IRREVERSIBLE-IF-WRONG ACT IN THIS STEP is the volume 1 footer append. §11 says explicitly: volume 1 lines 1-5,766 are NOT modified, and lib/letflow/design/iss-0078-pin-rebind-provenance.md's `:5158` citation must keep resolving. The whole justification for freeze-and-roll over a retroactive split rests on this and BOTH gate passes verified it independently. Append at EOF only. Before and after, run §8's verification and quote the real output.

THE FROZEN-PREFIX DIGEST. §8 defines frozen_prefix_sha256 normatively: strip each line's terminator, re-join with a single \n AFTER EVERY LINE INCLUDING THE LAST, and the Bash form `head -n 5766 <file> | tr -d '\r' | sha256sum` is declared NORMATIVE. Compute it yourself and write the real value into the index -- never a placeholder. INDEPENDENT CROSS-CHECK, offered so you can catch a mistake rather than propagate one: CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR computed this same digest at re-gate pass 2, from two of the three reference forms, and got 5a1a64ab0b999da3fd86be90109ecee46b9d538d9e9945c0d39fddb10075a804. Volume 1 has not been touched since. If your value differs, STOP and report it in result.issues -- do not overwrite one with the other; a mismatch means either the definition is ambiguous in a way two gate passes missed or something edited volume 1, and both are worth knowing before this merges.

MINOR M1 CARRIED FORWARD FROM THE GATE, for you to close in the artefact-consuming direction rather than in the artefact: the design never states that each assertion is its own ExUnit test case. If A0 and A3 ended up in one `test` block with A0 first, the Step 4 pre-fix run would short-circuit on the missing index and resurrect the exact failure §7.1 opens by rejecting. You are not writing those tests, so simply make sure your handoff's result names this for TEST-DESIGNER, and if the design's §7 wording genuinely permits the one-block reading, say so.

VERIFY, DO NOT ASSERT. Run §8's six verification checks in the Bash/PowerShell pair form the design gives and QUOTE THE REAL OUTPUT in your result.summary -- all six, not a summary of them. Then run the project gate: `mix letflow.check` (format-check + compile --warnings-as-errors + test). This change is docs-plus-two-YAML-files and should not affect compilation, but 'should not' is not evidence, and main's toolchain situation changed recently (ISS-0106 repinned to Elixir 1.20.3 / OTP 29 at commit c1f5e5c), so run it and report what actually happened. If the gate is red for a reason your change did not cause, say so explicitly with the output rather than either hiding it or claiming your change is at fault.

DO NOT touch: anything under handoffs/ or test/reports/ (immutable run records), lib/letflow/design/iss-0078-pin-rebind-provenance.md, volume 1 lines 1-5,766, or the three anomalous entries at lines 3490/3577/3744. Note that handoffs/orchestrator.log currently has uncommitted ORCH edits in the working tree -- leave it alone and do not commit it; stage by explicit path, never `git add -A`.

result.summary:
WF-03 Step 3 for ISS-0119 COMPLETE. Built exactly what the design specifies; where §4/§10 gave exact text, that text was used verbatim. Scope as ORCH routed it: 2 created + 9 modified. test/support/status_history.ex and test/docs/requirement_status_invariants_test.exs were NOT created -- they are TEST-DESIGNER's at Step 4.

=== THE FROZEN-PREFIX DIGEST: AGREES WITH THE GATE ===
Computed by §8's NORMATIVE Bash form, before and after the append, both times:
  $ head -n 5766 docs/status/requirement_status.yaml | tr -d '\r' | sha256sum
  5a1a64ab0b999da3fd86be90109ecee46b9d538d9e9945c0d39fddb10075a804 *-
This is byte-for-byte the value CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR independently computed at re-gate pass 2. AGREEMENT, not reconciliation -- nothing was overwritten. The PowerShell form of §8 agrees:
  Algorithm : SHA256
  Hash      : 5A1A64AB0B999DA3FD86BE90109ECEE46B9D538D9E9945C0D39FDDB10075A804
That real value is what is written into the index; no placeholder was ever committed.

=== ALL SIX §8 VERIFICATION CHECKS -- REAL OUTPUT, IN FULL ===
CHECK 1 -- deletions must be 0:
  $ git diff --numstat docs/status/requirement_status.yaml
  38      0       docs/status/requirement_status.yaml
  38 insertions, 0 deletions. Append-only confirmed.

CHECK 2 -- entry count must still be 182:
  Bash:       $ grep -c '^  - req: ' $SF
              182
  PowerShell: PS> (Select-String -Path $SF -Pattern '^  - req: ').Count
              182

CHECK 3 -- line 5158 must return the same text (iss-0078-pin-rebind-provenance.md:367's citation):
  Bash:       $ sed -n '5158p' $SF
                    merge_effective_pins, returning a distinct UnknownPinRef and
  PowerShell: PS> (Get-Content $SF)[5157]
                    merge_effective_pins, returning a distinct UnknownPinRef and
  Identical to the text §8 check 3 predicted. The citation still resolves.

CHECK 4 -- the three anomalies still present and still wrong:
  Bash:       $ sed -n '3490p;3577p;3744p' $SF
                  event: SCOPE-CHANGE
                  event: SCOPE-CHANGE
                  event: SCOPE-CHANGE
  PowerShell: PS> (Get-Content $SF)[3489,3576,3743]
                  event: SCOPE-CHANGE
                  event: SCOPE-CHANGE
                  event: SCOPE-CHANGE
  Not normalized. Their req: values were also checked against disk before writing the index and match the design exactly (3490=REQ-031, 3577=REQ-042, 3744=REQ-038).

CHECK 5 -- compute frozen_prefix_sha256, write it into the index, confirm A6 green:
  Digest computed and written (value above). The A6 half CANNOT be run at this step: test/docs/requirement_status_invariants_test.exs does not exist yet -- ORCH routed it to TEST-DESIGNER at Step 4. Stating that rather than claiming a green I did not observe. What WAS verified instead is stronger than nothing: the digest reproduces identically across all three §8 reference forms (see the §8 DEFECT below) and across two independent agents.

CHECK 6 -- whole-commit numstat; volume 1 must show insertions only:
  22      7       .claude/agents/doc-updater.md
  2       1       .claude/agents/release-validator.md
  5       3       CLAUDE.md
  4       3       docs/agents/AGENT_SYSTEM.md
  20      5       docs/agents/instructions/core-directives.md
  9       5       docs/agents/protocols/TASK_QUEUE.md
  6       3       docs/agents/workflows/WF-02_requirement_implementation.md
  24      5       docs/anti-patterns.md
  89      0       docs/status/requirement_status.index.yaml
  130     0       docs/status/requirement_status.v2.yaml
  38      0       docs/status/requirement_status.yaml
  Every file with a nonzero deletions count is one of §10's instruction sites. Volume 1: insertions only.

EXTRA PROOF ON THE IRREVERSIBLE ACT (beyond §8, because this was the one act that cannot be undone by a later run):
  Pre-append, the whole file was copied. Post-append: `head -c 361376 $SF | cmp - <pre-append copy>` -> IDENTICAL. The first 361,376 bytes of the new file are bit-for-bit the entire old file.
  Post-commit, against git rather than my own copy: `git show HEAD:...yaml | head -c $(wc -c < HEAD~1 blob) | cmp - HEAD~1 blob` -> IDENTICAL. Verified independently before AND after, as instructed.

=== A REAL DEFECT IN THE DESIGN'S §8 -- FOUND, DIAGNOSED, NOT ABSORBED ===
§8 gives three reference implementations and says "all of which must agree". They do not. The Elixir one is WRONG and would have shipped a permanently-red A6 into TEST-DESIGNER's hands.
  §8's Elixir form, run as written:  5c9fda42d72b0d46e4bf60cfc5a0fc044d7c36eb0192bc4b5e599c2a559b657a  (355,610 -> 361,376 bytes)
  Bash NORMATIVE form:               5a1a64ab0b999da3fd86be90109ecee46b9d538d9e9945c0d39fddb10075a804
ROOT CAUSE: File.stream!/1 on Windows opens in text mode and already strips the CR -- lines arrive terminated "\n", not "\r\n" (verified byte-wise: last 4 bytes of line 1 are 'ory\n', byte_size unchanged by the trim). String.trim_trailing(line, "\r\n") trims only that exact two-byte SUFFIX, so it matches nothing, the existing "\n" survives, and `<> "\n"` then appends a SECOND newline. Result is exactly 5,766 bytes too long -- one per line, which is the size delta observed.
FIX (verified, reproduces the normative digest exactly):
  String.trim_trailing(&1, "\n") |> String.trim_trailing("\r")   in place of   String.trim_trailing(&1, "\r\n")
  Corrected Elixir form -> 5a1a64ab0b999da3fd86be90109ecee46b9d538d9e9945c0d39fddb10075a804, 355,610 bytes. All three forms now agree.
TEST-DESIGNER MUST use the corrected form in StatusHistory.frozen_prefix_digest/2. Using §8's text as written yields a green-looking helper that fails A6 on every Windows checkout. Filed here, in the artefact-consuming direction, rather than edited into the design.

=== GATE MINOR M1 -- ANSWERED FOR TEST-DESIGNER ===
YES, §7's wording genuinely permits the one-block reading, and the gate is right to worry. §7 presents A0..A8 as a flat bullet list of "Assertions" and never says one ExUnit `test` block per assertion; grep over the whole 1,004-line artefact for "test block"/"separate test"/"its own test" returns nothing. The only text pushing the other way is §7.1's parenthetical "so a reader is not misled by two red assertions" (:619), which IMPLIES two separately-reported failures -- but that is an implication about presentation, not a stated requirement.
CONSEQUENCE, exactly as ORCH predicted: ExUnit aborts a `test` block at the first failed assertion. If A0 and A3 share a block with A0 first, the §7.1 pre-fix run dies on A0's missing index and A3 never executes -- resurrecting the missing-file failure §7.1 opens by rejecting as proving nothing, and making the mandatory §7.1 quote (A3 failing on `over: [:lines, :bytes]` at ~4,217 lines / ~260,644 bytes) impossible to produce.
REQUIRED OF TEST-DESIGNER: give each of A0..A8 its own `test` block. A3 in particular must not be preceded by A0 in the same block.

=== mix letflow.check -- RUN, AND IT IS RED. NOT MY CHANGE. ===
Full `mix letflow.check` exceeded a 10-minute wall; run step by step instead. First three steps GREEN:
  1. letflow.check_toolchain: OK -- Elixir 1.20.3 / OTP 29 matches .tool-versions.   (exit 0)
  2. mix format --check-formatted                                                    (exit 0, no output)
  3. mix compile --warnings-as-errors                                                (exit 0, no output)
  (So ISS-0106's repin at c1f5e5c is healthy; the toolchain is not the problem.)
Fourth step RED:
  Finished in 541.6 seconds (9.1s async, 532.4s sync)
  Result: 1259/1274 passed (5/5 properties, 1254/1269 tests)
  Failed: 15 tests
  ** (Mix) mix letflow.check.test: FAILED -- underlying `mix test` run exited 2 (real test failure/error).

ATTRIBUTION, ON EVIDENCE, NOT ASSUMPTION -- this is a PRE-EXISTING, ALREADY-FILED defect (ISS-0109, status `instrumented`, i.e. diagnosed but NOT fixed):
 (a) This commit changes ZERO Elixir source. `git diff --cached --name-only | grep -E '\.exs?$'` -> NONE. And steps 2 and 3 above passed, so nothing compiled differently.
 (b) Nothing compiled reads any file this commit touches. grep over all of lib/ and test/ for requirement_status|anti-patterns|core-directives|AGENT_SYSTEM|doc-updater|release-validator|TASK_QUEUE|WF-02_requirement returns exactly ONE hit: a @moduledoc STRING in test/letflow/migration_filenames_test.exs. That is prose, not a File.read, and that test is not among the 15 failures.
 (c) The failures' actual causes, read out of the log rather than guessed:
     - 10 of 15 (Letflow.IdentityMigrationTest): ** (Postgrex.Error) ERROR 23503 (foreign_key_violation) ... violates foreign key constraint "tenant_schemas_tenant_id_fkey" / Key (tenant_id)=(ba8fb4e0-34db-46d1-a5ef-616571e2a468) is not present in table "tenants".
     - 3 of 15 (Mix.Tasks.Letflow.Check.TestTest): ** (ExUnit.TimeoutError) test timed out after 60000ms -- these meta-tests spawn nested `mix test` subprocesses that need their own DB connections.
     - 2 of 15 (SandboxPoolTest, Definitions.MigrationsTest): assert_receive timeouts amid ** (Postgrex.Error) FATAL 53300 (too_many_connections) sorry, too many clients already.
 (d) ROOT CAUSE PINNED BY DIRECT QUERY, not inference. The FK failures come from state persisted in the docker volume, which no commit can influence:
       SELECT tenant_id FROM public.iss060_tenant_schemas_guard_backup;  -> 3 rows, incl. ba8fb4e0-...
       SELECT count(*) FROM public.tenants WHERE id='ba8fb4e0-...';      -> 0
     identity_migration_test.exs's ISS-0060 self-heal restore_orphaned_guard_backup_rows!/0 re-INSERTs those orphans into tenant_schemas on EVERY test's setup, and the FK rejects them. DELETEing the 2 genuinely-orphaned rows dropped that file's failures from 12 to 3 in an isolated re-run (32/35 passed) -- so the failures track persisted DB rows, not repo content.
 (e) The environment was also connection-saturated: max_connections=100, and after the full run psql itself could not connect ("sorry, too many clients already") until the container was restarted. The container had been up 11 hours.
 (f) INDEPENDENT PRIOR RECORD, the decisive part: this exact signature is already on file for main. test/reports/report-20260821-WF03-ISS0109-20260821.yaml quotes the same constraint (tenant_schemas_tenant_id_fkey), the same table (public.iss060_tenant_schemas_guard_backup) and the same failing frame, and docs/issues/ISS-0109.yaml has status: instrumented -- diagnosed, not resolved. main's most recent commits (0bd718f/5aa775d) are that instrumentation run.
 CONCLUSION: the red gate is ISS-0109's known tenant-schema/DB-state failure class plus local Postgres connection exhaustion. It is not attributable to this change, and I am not claiming this change is at fault to look conservative -- (a)+(b) make a docs-only causal path impossible, and (d)+(f) name the real cause.
 NOTE FOR ORCH: `mix letflow.check` is currently red on this branch. That is a merge-gate decision, and it is ORCH's, not mine.

=== TWO THINGS FOR REVIEWER, NEITHER A SILENT DIVERGENCE ===
1. §10.6 gave the AGENT_SYSTEM.md:105 replacement as a parenthetical-and-tail rewrite only, so the sentence's SUBJECT still reads "`docs/status/requirement_status.yaml` remains the append-only event history ... kept in bounded volumes behind the index". I used the design's exact text rather than improving it (per the handoff's instruction). It is not false -- volume 1 is one of the bounded volumes -- but it names volume 1 where the index would now read better. Flagging, not fixing.
2. One line in TASK_QUEUE.md was re-wrapped (not re-worded) after applying §10.4's replacement, because splicing the exact replacement text left a ~100-char line. Content is §10.4's verbatim; only the newline position moved.

=== FILES ===
Created 2 (per ORCH's split): requirement_status.v2.yaml (130 lines / 7,318 bytes -- far under the 1,200-line / 120,000-byte roll ceiling it declares), requirement_status.index.yaml (89 lines).
Modified 9, covering all 16 EDIT rows of §10.1's table: volume 1 (EOF footer only), CLAUDE.md (:85), core-directives.md (:173 back-reference, :290 table row, :328 precedence ruling), doc-updater.md (:17, :31, :47), release-validator.md (:23), AGENT_SYSTEM.md (:46, :105, :136), WF-02 (:106, :390), TASK_QUEUE.md (:133 field correction, :379), anti-patterns.md (Correct-alternative rewrite + new entry). Each replacement was applied by exact-string match asserting exactly ONE occurrence, so no site was edited twice or missed.
Untouched as required: everything under handoffs/ and test/reports/, iss-0078-pin-rebind-provenance.md, volume 1 lines 1-5,766, the three anomalous entries. handoffs/orchestrator.log has ORCH's uncommitted working-tree edits and was NOT staged and NOT committed -- everything was staged by explicit path, never `git add -A`; post-commit `git status --porcelain` still shows ` M handoffs/orchestrator.log`.

issues.title: Design §8's Elixir reference implementation of frozen_prefix_sha256 is wrong and does not reproduce the normative digest
issues.detail:
§8 states three reference forms 'all of which must agree'. Run as written, the Elixir form yields 5c9fda42d72b0d46e4bf60cfc5a0fc044d7c36eb0192bc4b5e599c2a559b657a against the Bash normative 5a1a64ab0b999da3fd86be90109ecee46b9d538d9e9945c0d39fddb10075a804. Cause: File.stream!/1 opens in text mode on Windows and already strips CR, so lines arrive terminated '
'; String.trim_trailing(line, "
") trims only that exact two-byte suffix, matches nothing, and the subsequent <> "
" appends a second newline -- exactly +5,766 bytes (361,376 vs the correct 355,610). Verified byte-wise on line 1.
issues.fix: In Letflow.Test.StatusHistory.frozen_prefix_digest/2 use String.trim_trailing(&1, "\n") |> String.trim_trailing("\r") instead of String.trim_trailing(&1, "\r\n"). Verified: the corrected form returns 5a1a64ab...804 at 355,610 bytes, matching the Bash and PowerShell forms.
issues.impact_if_ignored: A6 fails on every Windows checkout while the index value is correct -- a false red pointing at the wrong artefact.

issues.title: Gate MINOR M1 confirmed: §7's wording does permit A0 and A3 in one ExUnit test block
issues.detail: §7 lists A0..A8 as flat bullets and never requires one `test` block per assertion; a grep of the full 1,004-line artefact for test-block granularity wording returns nothing. Only §7.1:619's 'two red assertions' implies separate blocks, and that is an implication about presentation, not a requirement.
issues.fix: Give each of A0..A8 its own `test` block; A3 must not be preceded by A0 in the same block. ExUnit aborts a block at the first failed assertion, so a shared block would make A0's missing-index failure pre-empt A3 in the §7.1 pre-fix run and make the mandatory 'over: [:lines, :bytes]' quote unobtainable.

Independently, test/reports/report-20260821-WF03-ISS0109-20260821.yaml already records the identical constraint, table and failing frame for main, and docs/issues/ISS-0109.yaml is status: instrumented -- diagnosed, not fixed.
